Nora Patel: OrionHealth filed SUP-6344 asking for SLA credit and burst-waiver after p99 spikes during Mar19 maintenance. Invoice shows 24 GPU-hrs burst ($2,880) and reserved month $12,000.
Evan Reed: incident timeline: kernel patch -> queueing -> rollback. Impact ~72 minutes; partner throttling caused extra burst ~10 GPU-hrs.
Sophie Tran: policy calc: SLA credit = 72/44640 * $12,000 = $19.38. Customer objects that burst was forced by failover, asking to waive.
Nora Patel: propose applying policy SLA credit ($19.38) + discretionary waiver for 8 of 10 burst hours (~$960) = total $979.38. Need finance ops OK.
Evan Reed: cost impact: partner billed 10 hrs @ $70/hr = $700; if we waive 8 hrs we absorb $560. Recommend absorb as retention gesture.
Sophie Tran: approving discretionary waiver up to $1,000. @billing-bot create ADJ-2026-4510 with artifacts: SUP-6344, incident-log, partner-report.
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4510 created. Status: pending-discretionary-approval.
Nora Patel: great — please schedule for Apr billing run once approved and draft customer note: "SLA credit applied per policy; one-time goodwill waiver for burst overage."
billing-bot: ADJ-2026-4510 status updated: approved_by_finance_ops. Scheduled for billing run 2026-04-03. Journal JE-2026-7821 created. Customer notified.
Sophie Tran: internal follow-ups: open partner dispute for throttling (PD-212) and consider adding a minimum credit floor to SLA docs.
Nora Patel: thanks team. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
